claims.text: EF Core docs: Add/AddAsync marks a new entity as a tracked change; SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync issues an INSERT for Added entities and an UPDATE for Modified ones, and the data reaches the database only when that call runs.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/saving/basic.md, "Adding Data" and "Updating Data"

claims.text: EF Core docs: for most database providers, SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync wraps all changes in a single call in one transaction by default; if any change fails, the transaction is rolled back and none of the changes are applied.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/saving/basic.md "Multiple operations"; entity-framework/core/saving/transactions.md "Default transaction behavior"

claims.text: EF Core docs: by convention, a non-composite primary key of type int (among others) is set up to have its value generated by the database for inserted entities if the application doesn't provide one; the database provider configures the underlying mechanism (an identity column, for PostgreSQL).

OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync builds an Order, calls AddAsync(order) then SaveChangesAsync(), then notifier.Send(order.Id, ...) and returns order; order.Id is unset before these calls. repository/notifier are primary-constructor parameters of OrderService.
EfOrderRepository.AddAsync and SaveChangesAsync are one-line wrappers calling db.Orders.AddAsync and db.SaveChangesAsync directly.

Live run against the stage-1 lab: POST /api/v1/orders with a valid body returns 201 with a real, nonzero id in both the JSON body's id field and the Location header's trailing path segment, though the request body never supplies an id.
claims.source_hint: live run this session: curl POST /api/v1/auth/login + POST /api/v1/orders

claims.text: EF Core docs: some forms of value generation may access the database to generate a key value (the only such generator shipping with EF Core is HiLoValueGenerator); AddAsync exists to support that case, but with an identity-column key like orders.id, no database access happens at that point.

EF Core docs: an Added entity gets a temporary key value stored in the change tracker, not set onto the entity instance directly; real key values are read back from the database once SaveChanges runs, and only then set onto the entity instance.

By default, one SaveChanges call saves its staged changes all-or-nothing, independently of any other call, so a later call can't undo what an earlier one saved; manual transaction control (DbContext.Database API) can share one transaction across calls instead.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/saving/transactions.md, "Default transaction behavior" and "Controlling transactions"

claims.text: EF Core docs: Add/Attach/Update work on the full graph of entities passed to them, so adding an Order also tracks its OrderItems as Added, not just the Order itself.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/saving/basic.md TIP under "Adding Data"; entity-framework/core/saving/related-data.md

claims.text: db/schema.sql at stage-1: customers, products, orders, payments, and notifications each declare a single-column identity id primary key; order_items is keyed by the pair (order_id, product_id) instead, with no identity column.
